title: A Verdict for the Portrait
premise: True-crime podcaster Noor Lockridge built her reputation closing cold cases no one else would touch, so when a letter arrives confessing to the 1994 murder of painter Vivienne Ashcombe—postmarked the day after Vivienne's estranged daughter's funeral—Noor sees one last impossible case. The confession is signed by a man who died in 2001, and every alibi in the old file was manufactured by the Ashcombe family's lawyers to protect the estate's inheritance. As Noor interviews the surviving heirs, she discovers Vivienne's final portrait, long believed lost, contains a hidden underpainting that names her killer. In the end, Noor exposes the family matriarch's surviving sister as the murderer and forger of the dead man's confession, choosing to broadcast the truth even though it destroys the legacy—and the inheritance—she herself unknowingly stands to inherit.
about_author: Elodie Underhill is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate papers in country houses before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about what families preserve, conceal, and quietly burn.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Noor Lockridge, POV. Days after wrapping her most successful season, Noor receives a confession letter for the thirty-year-old Ashcombe murder, postmarked the day after the victim's daughter's funeral. The signature belongs to a man dead since 2001. Emotional beat: uneasy fascination—the case feels like it has been waiting for her.

chapters.title: The Coldest File
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. She pulls every scrap on the 1994 killing: Vivienne Ashcombe found strangled in her studio, a handyman convicted in absentia after fleeing, an estate worth millions sealed in trust. Noor notices the alibis share one lawyer's fingerprints. Emotional beat: professional hunger sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ashcombe House Keeps Its Silence
chapters.summary: Noor, POV, arriving at the decaying estate. She meets the surviving sister, Marguerite Ashcombe, now eighty and magnetic, who grants an interview that is really a performance. A locked studio door dominates the hallway. Emotional beat: charm with teeth beneath it.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Cross-referencing the funeral guest list against the original statements, she finds three heirs whose timelines were 'corrected' by the same solicitor. One heir, cousin Theo, admits he lied—but about something smaller, or so he claims. Emotional beat: first crack in the wall.

chapters.title: What the Daughter Burned
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: flashbacks from the dead daughter, Camille, via her journals recovered by an estate sale dealer. Camille suspected the confession letter existed and spent her last years hunting it. Emotional beat: grief reframed as unfinished investigation.

chapters.title: A Podcast Named Accomplice
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Her producer warns the series could be defamation bait; the family's lawyer sends a cease-and-desist before episode one airs. Noor realizes someone inside the house is feeding her documents. Emotional beat: paranoia braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Handyman Who Ran
chapters.summary: Noor, POV, tracking the convicted handyman's trail—he died homeless in 2019, but his letters claim he fled because he saw 'the second shadow' in the studio window. Emotional beat: pity for the scapegoat, dread of what he witnessed.

chapters.title: Marguerite Remembers Everything
chapters.summary: Second interview with Marguerite, whose flawless memory begins contradicting itself only around the night of the murder. She gifts Noor a small sketch—Vivienne's last study. Emotional beat: admiration curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Underpainting
chapters.summary: Conservator POV (guest expert, Dr. Ilsa Ren). X-ray analysis of the study reveals a hidden layer beneath: a partial figure and painted letters. Someone has already tried to scrape it once. Emotional beat: revelation as physical evidence.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. The will's strange condition surfaces: the trust dissolves if Vivienne's death is legally reclassified. Whoever killed her had everything to gain from a quick conviction. Emotional beat: motive crystallizing into architecture.

chapters.title: Theo's Second Lie
chapters.summary: Noor confronts Theo, who breaks down: he was in the house that night, saw Marguerite leave the studio wing, and was paid to forget. His alibi was purchased. Emotional beat: betrayal and terror of reprisal.

chapters.title: Letters from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Document examiner POV. The confession's handwriting is genuine—but traced over years of practice sheets found in Marguerite's late husband's effects. The forger learned to be him. Emotional beat: the impossible made methodical.

chapters.title: Why Confess Now
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. The postmark date aligns with the funeral because Camille's death triggered the trust's final review—someone needed the case closed on their terms before auditors arrived. Emotional beat: the killer is racing her.

chapters.title: The Locked Studio
chapters.summary: Noor breaks into Vivienne's sealed studio at night and finds the great final portrait missing from its frame—only a clean rectangle of unfaded wall. Footsteps above. Emotional beat: violation and vertigo; she is not alone in the past.

chapters.title: Threats in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Her archive copies vanish; her car's brakes are tampered with; the producer quits under pressure. Marguerite offers her money and a place in the family story instead. Emotional beat: fear met with temptation.

chapters.title: Camille's Last Tape
chapters.summary: A mailed package arrives: Camille's dictaphone tape, recorded the week she died, naming the portrait's hiding place at the chapel and whispering 'she taught me to paint, then taught me to lie.' Emotional beat: the dead reaching across time.

chapters.title: Chapel Vault
chapters.summary: Noor and Theo recover the portrait from behind the chapel altar. Under raking light, the underpainting resolves: Marguerite's face, and Vivienne's hand spelling a name. Emotional beat: triumph immediately shadowed by danger.

chapters.title: The Second Shadow
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Marguerite catches them at the house; Theo flees; Noor is held at knifepoint while Marguerite explains the inheritance, the framed handyman, and the forged confession meant to bury the case forever. Emotional beat: power fully unmasked.

chapters.title: Verdict in the Studio
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Noor, live-streaming from her pocket, provokes Marguerite into a full confession before police arrive—drawn by the tampered-brakes report Noor filed days earlier. Emotional beat: the recorder as weapon; invisibility turned to advantage.

chapters.title: Reclassification
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Legal machinery grinds: conviction vacated, case reopened, trust frozen. Marguerite, charged at last, remains serene—power refusing to admit decay. Emotional beat: justice as slow, unsatisfying arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Portrait Restored
chapters.summary: Dr. Ren completes conservation; the finished portrait goes on public view, Vivienne's hidden accusation finally legible. Noor declines the family's settlement and any inheritance claim. Emotional beat: memory given back its voice.

chapters.title: One Case She Couldn't Close
chapters.summary: Final Noor POV. Recording the season finale, Noor admits the case closed her more than she closed it: she learned she was Camille's unnamed heir all along, and chose truth over legacy. Final beat: quiet, earned peace—and a new letter on her desk.
